To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the over-expression in Arabidopsis of a bacterial phytase leads to a significant reduction in the seed phytic acid (PA), without any effect on seed germination potential, and to an increase in in vivo phosphate and sulfate contents and in plant biomass production after phosphate limitation.

the over-expression (OX) of the bacterial phytic acid (PA)-degrading enzyme phytase PHY in Arabidopsis thaliana leads to the reduction of PA in seeds, without affecting the seed germination, but with an increased mobilization of free iron.

the over-expression in Arabidopsis of a bacterial phytase gene reduces the concentration of seed phytate, and reveals its involvement, in addition to iron homeostasis, in the regulation of phosphate and sulfate homeostasis and signalling.

the role of PA in plant metabolism and provides a new insight in the understanding of the role of PA reserves in plant development.
a new approach to improve the nutritional value of seeds and to enhance plant phosphate and sulfate homeostasis and tolerance to phosphate starvation.
the development of a new approach to improve the nutritional quality of plants by decreasing their PA content without affecting their growth capacity.

PA is a key element in the regulation of phosphate homeostasis, signaling, and plant development.

the over-expression strategy can be used to engineer plants with low PA concentration, and that PA plays a role in the regulation of plant growth and in the maintenance of ion homeostasis.
